Dear Dr. Mercer,

Thank you for evaluating this 10-month-old boy who was referred to our clinic due to complex multisystem concerns that have been evolving since birth. He lives at home with his parents and an older sister. The family history is unremarkable, with no known parental consanguinity. 

The infant demonstrates marked failure to thrive and a poorly nourished state despite high-calorie formula supplementation. He is persistently fussy and inconsolable, demonstrating significant distress and articular pain upon manipulation of his limbs. On musculoskeletal examination, he has marked limitation in passive range of motion with fixed flexion deformities involving his knees and elbows. Inspection of his oral cavity reveals notable fleshy enlargement and thickening of the gums. His skin examination is notable for scattered small red bumps on his trunk, as well as distinct, firm, indurated plaques of thickened skin over his thighs. His cardiopulmonary exam is otherwise normal, with clear breath sounds and regular heart rhythm without murmurs.

Recent laboratory investigations highlighted a depressed serum sodium level of 131 mEq/L and a severely low serum albumin of 2.1 g/dL. Further stool testing confirmed significant enteric protein wasting accounting for his hypoalbuminemic state. His renal function, liver enzymes, and complete blood count have otherwise remained within normal limits.

Given the progression of these clinical findings, I would greatly appreciate your assessment and recommendations regarding a unifying explanation and subsequent management. 

Sincerely,
Dr. Julian Vance
